alignments.note: Substantival article before a participle with a single English word: rule 90 gives the relativizer to the article, the participle keeping its own verb.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied determiner: rule 51's closing clause makes *a* a helper on the noun.

The ASV recasts the appositional phrase with a supplied verb; rule 92 puts the supplied words on the expressed predicate noun and leaves the article its bare determiner. Head on *testimony*, the word realizing the lexeme, the supplied *to be borne* realizing no source token.
Rule 21's determinerless clause: the supplied case preposition *in* rides with the dative noun, discontinuously under rule 15.
Rule 47: ἴδιος is a source word able to take the supplied possessive, and here the noun is anarthrous so nothing competes.

review_notes: The supplied *to be borne* was kept on μαρτύριον under rule 92 rather than on the dative time phrase; nothing else in the appositional phrase is left unspent to carry it.
